findings.issue: Still open from round 1, but narrow. decide() classes any rule that ROLE_CUSTOMER passes as AUTHENTICATED. A future prefix rule such as hasRole("CUSTOMER") or hasAnyAuthority("ROLE_CUSTOMER", ...) would therefore be read as plain authenticated and would escape the new DENY/ROLE pin in rolePrefixesAreKnown. It is not an exposure (the rule is more restrictive), but the drift goes unnoticed.
findings.fix: Optional: also probe with an authenticated token that has no authorities (for example TestingAuthenticationToken with an empty authority list, setAuthenticated(true)). Only class a rule as AUTHENTICATED if that token passes; otherwise class it as ROLE and include ROLE_CUSTOMER in the admitted set.

findings.issue: Carried over and deliberately skipped by the engineer: field()/hasField() hand-roll a walk up the class hierarchy that Spring's ReflectionUtils.findField already provides. Entry also re-parses the pattern string instead of using the reflected PathPattern.
findings.fix: Optional: use ReflectionUtils.findField, and store the reflected PathPattern in Entry.

findings.issue: rawStatus prints a 'PROBE ...' line for every request, and the new code uses inline fully qualified names (java.time.Duration, java.util.function.Consumer, java.util.TreeMap) where imports would be the usual style.
findings.fix: Optional: drop the println or route it through the assertion description, and import the types.

summary: Round 2 (delta e87cc80..57e9c94) fixes round-1 minors 1-3 and nit 6. (1) rolePrefixesAreKnown now pins every DENY and ROLE entry by method and pattern to exactly {ANY /actuator/** -> DENY, ANY /api/admin/** -> ROLE[4 authorities]}. A new denyAll, or a rule for a role outside the probe set (which reads as DENY), now fails. The expected string is built with TreeSet ordering, which matches Decision.toString over the TreeSet-ordered roles. (2) EdgeRules.requireSupportedMatcher allows a non-Or matcher only at the last index and otherwise throws 'EdgeRules could not read the chain: unsupported matcher ... at index n'. A new EdgeRulesTest case covers it. (3) Tokens are minted through the new TestKeys.accessTokenValidFor with a 6 h lifetime. It reuses the existing private token() with ISSUER/AUDIENCE, which removes the 600 s timing flake. (6) The stale phase9.md progress phrase is removed. PRIVILEGED now uses the Roles.ROLE_* constants. The security follow-ups are added as real-Netty probes with raw URIs: 8 traversal probes starting from permit prefixes are asserted to be exactly 400; /api/sellers/me trailing-slash and path-parameter variants are asserted to be 400 or 401; _method and X-HTTP-Method-Override on a protected POST, and HEAD /api/sellers/me, are asserted to be 401. The engineer recorded the observed statuses, and none of them is a pass-through. The reviewed-permit reasons now state the rate-limit position honestly, and the /api/auth exemption is deferred to the backlog. Still no src/main or build.gradle diff (git diff --exit-code is recorded). The engineer's evidence.md records 1277 contract tests and 7 EdgeRulesTest tests passing and forge-verify --changed PASS. I did not run the tests myself. What remains is one minor (a CUSTOMER-admitting role rule would be read as AUTHENTICATED; more restrictive, not an exposure) and optional nits, so approve.
